record.paper_title: Statements and open problems on decidable sets X ⊆ N that contain informal notions and refer to the current knowledge on X
record.context_brief: Threshold number for primes of the form n^2 + 1
record.original_question: Is there a known threshold number for the set P_{n^2+1} of primes of the form n^2 + 1? In the paper's terminology, this asks whether there exists a known integer n such that, if P_{n^2+1} is finite, then every prime of the form m^2 + 1 belongs to (−∞, n].

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4. Is there a known threshold number of Pn^2+1?

Definition 3.3. We say that an integer n is a threshold number of a set X ⊆ N, if
card(X) < ω ⇒ X ⊆ (−∞, n].

Edmund Landau’s conjecture states that the set Pn^2+1 of primes of the form n^2 + 1 is
infinite, see [13], [14], [16].

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P = { p ∈ ℕ : p is prime and p = m² + 1 for some m ∈ ℕ }. Call an integer n a "threshold number" of a set X ⊆ ℕ if the implication

  |X| < ∞  ⟹  X ⊆ (−∞, n]

holds. Exhibit an explicit integer n that is provably a threshold number of P, or show that no such explicit n is currently known. Equivalently: produce a specific integer n with the property that if only finitely many primes of the form m² + 1 exist, then every such prime is at most n.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is tied to Landau's conjecture on the infinitude of primes of the form n²+1, which remains a famous open problem. No explicit, provable threshold integer n bounding all primes of the form m²+1 in the case of finiteness is known in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Landau's problems - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Are there infinitely many primes of the form n^2+1? This remains an unsolved problem.
status_evidence.claim: The infinitude of primes of the form n²+1 is an open problem, so no effective threshold is known.
